transcript.text: Mr. Lincoln. Representative Douglas has brought formal charges that you voted in favor of the Sangamon County land grant while simultaneously representing the principal beneficiary of that grant in your law practice. The ethics of this chamber require that no member profit from legislation he has a hand in passing. You are well-regarded here, sir, but I must hear your account. Explain yourself.

In the case of the Sangamon County land grant vote, it is true that I did vote in favor of it. However, I must stress that my decision was based solely on what I believed to be in the best interest of the people I represent, and not influenced by any personal gain for myself or my client.

As a lawyer, I do indeed have clients whom I represent in various legal matters. It is not uncommon for legislators to have ties to the legal profession. However, I take great care to ensure that my actions as a lawmaker are separate from my duties as an attorney. 

I understand the importance of upholding the integrity of this chamber and the trust of the people we serve. I can assure you that I take these responsibilities seriously and would never knowingly engage in any behavior that could be perceived as a conflict of interest.

I am willing to provide any additional information or clarification that may be needed to address these concerns. Thank you for allowing me the opportunity to speak on this matter.
